briefing:
# Canva Briefing: Meeting of 17 November 2026

## Purpose and Scope

This briefing prepares for a meeting with Canva on 17 November 2026. It covers developments from roughly 16 October to 15 November 2026, which is the 30-day window the request specifies. The dominant development in that window is a company-wide restructuring announced in early November. The sources reviewed contain no verified new hires, product launches, or acquisitions dated inside the window. Where older launches and deals are relevant as context, they are labelled as such. Sources differ on the exact announcement date (3 or 4 November), so this briefing gives the range.

## Executive Summary

- Canva announced a restructuring affecting 1,271 employees, about 22% of its workforce. The announcement came in a note from co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins, titled "An important update on our team" ([Canva, 2026](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/canva-team-update)).
- The restructuring merges Product, Growth and Platform into one product organisation, simplifies management layers, and concentrates more product teams in Sydney ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)).
- The 1,271 figure includes people who lose their role, change role, or are asked to relocate. Canva has not disclosed the number who will actually leave ([Newsweek, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)).
- Departing staff receive at least six months' salary ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)).
- A Capital Brief report, relayed by People Matters, says Canva could announce another round of redundancies or a company-wide hiring freeze in November ([People Matters, 2026](https://www.peoplematters.in/news/strategic-hr/canva-layoffs-in-november-company-reportedly-weighs-job-cuts-or-hiring-freeze-53137)). This is unconfirmed by Canva.

## What Changed in the Last 30 Days

### The Restructuring

Perkins wrote that Canva's growth has slowed for the first time in a decade and that small adjustments would not be enough to fix it ([Yahoo Finance, 2026](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/canva-first-growth-slowdown-decade-092457264.html)). The memo was reported as "without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history" ([UX UI Open, 2026](https://uxuiopen.com/blog/canva-layoff)).

Canva has described the changes as a simplification of a business that has become fragmented as it has grown. It has also stated that the restructuring is not a cost-cutting response to financial pressure ([Newsweek, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)). A Canva spokesperson said AI is not replacing the affected roles ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)).

The company has not published a breakdown of affected roles by job title, department, or country ([Newsweek, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)).

### Key Figures

| Metric | Figure | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Employees affected | 1,271 (about 22% of workforce) | [Newsweek, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250) |
| Minimum severance | At least six months' salary (about 26 weeks) | [Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations) |
| Technology sector average severance (2024) | 11.2 weeks | [Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations) |
| Expected revenue growth, 2026 | 20% year-on-year (revised from 30% in August) | [Newsweek, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250); [Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations) |
| Profitability | 2026 expected to be the 10th consecutive profitable year | [Newsweek, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250) |
| Expected office attendance | 2–3 days per week | [CTO Magazine, 2026](https://ctomagazine.com/canva-layoff-2026-workforce-restructuring-what-leaders-need-to-understand) |

### Timeline

| Date (2026) | Event | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 3 November | Restructuring announced; Newsweek reports the announcement on Tuesday, 3 November | [Newsweek, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250) |
| 3–4 November | Yahoo Finance reports the CEO note to staff on Wednesday; CTO Magazine dates publication to 4 November | [Yahoo Finance, 2026](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/canva-first-growth-slowdown-decade-092457264.html); [CTO Magazine, 2026](https://ctomagazine.com/canva-layoff-2026-workforce-restructuring-what-leaders-need-to-understand) |
| 3 November | People Matters reports a Capital Brief report on possible November cuts or hiring freeze | [People Matters, 2026](https://www.peoplematters.in/news/strategic-hr/canva-layoffs-in-november-company-reportedly-weighs-job-cuts-or-hiring-freeze-53137) |
| 10 November | Company-wide All Hands to discuss changes | [Canva, 2026](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/canva-team-update) |
| 11 November | Org All Hands begin; Org Leads brief their teams | [Canva, 2026](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/canva-team-update) |
| 12 November | CTO Magazine publishes analysis of the restructuring | [CTO Magazine, 2026](https://ctomagazine.com/canva-layoff-2026-workforce-restructuring-what-leaders-need-to-understand) |

Staff leaving Canva retain access to Slack and Gmail until the end of the week of the announcement, and leads were to share area-specific changes by the end of that week ([Canva, 2026](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/canva-team-update)).

### Hires

No new executive or senior hires were identified in the sources for the 30-day window.

### Launches

The sources do not contain a verified product launch dated within the 30-day window. The most recent product material reviewed is older and is therefore context only:

- **Canva Enterprise and workplace products.** Announced at Canva's first international Create event in Los Angeles. The launch included Canva Enterprise, a redesigned core experience, Canva Courses and Work Kits, and extension of the Affinity acquisition ([MarTech Cube, n.d.](https://www.martechcube.com/canva-launches-enterprise-era-with-new-workplace-products)). Canva reported more than 185 million monthly active users and more than $2.3 billion in annualised revenue at that event ([MarTech Cube, n.d.](https://www.martechcube.com/canva-launches-enterprise-era-with-new-workplace-products)). The event date is not stated in the source, and the general availability timing ("August") suggests a date earlier in 2026.
- **Creative Operating System.** A broader launch including Video 2.0, Canva Forms, Sheets, Code integration and the Canva Design Model, available through ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. Affinity was reported as now free for everyone ([Analytics India Magazine, n.d.](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/analytics-india-magazine_canva-has-launched-its-creative-operating-activity-7389930813032804353-fmu0)). The date is not provided.

### Deals

No new acquisitions were identified inside the window. Context from earlier deals:

- **Simtheory and Ortto.** Canva acquired Simtheory, an AI workspace and collaboration platform, and Ortto, a customer data and marketing automation company. Ortto has more than 11,000 customers across 190 countries ([Demand Gen Report, 2026](https://www.demandgenreport.com/industry-news/news-brief/canva-acquisitions-expands-marketing-ai-capabilities/52546)). This deal was published on 22 April 2026, outside the window.
- **Flourish.** Flourish, a data visualisation platform, joined the Canva family. Flourish reported more than 750,000 users who had made more than 7.5 million visuals ([Flourish, n.d.](https://flourish.studio/blog/flourish-canva)). The date is not stated in the source.

## Analysis

### Strategic Rationale

Canva's stated rationale is consistent with a growth slowdown. Growth is reported to have slowed for the first time in a decade, and the company has cut its 2026 forecast from 30% to 20% ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)). Niehues argues that the bottleneck is handover latency, since every product improvement had to be agreed between Product, Growth and Platform ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)). A LinkedIn commentator with growth-leadership experience makes a similar argument, stating that "growth is no longer a department" and that separate teams become a cost once AI shortens testing cycles ([LinkedIn, n.d.](https://www.linkedin.com/news/story/canva-announces-restructuring-affecting-over-1200-jobs-7754140)).

### Our Assessment

In our view, the organisational logic is credible, but the headline figures overstate the scale of job loss. The 1,271 figure combines exits, role changes and relocations, and Canva has not said how many people will leave ([Newsweek, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)). Relocation to Sydney is therefore a significant part of the headline number, and it may function as a soft attrition mechanism. The six-month severance floor is generous relative to the sector average of 11.2 weeks ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)). Public commentary has praised it ([Newsweek, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)), but it also signals that management expects a sizeable number of exits.

The framing "not cost-cutting" should be tested. Canva remains profitable and reports strong scale, with $2.3 billion in annualised revenue ([MarTech Cube, n.d.](https://www.martechcube.com/canva-launches-enterprise-era-with-new-workplace-products)). These facts support the claim that the restructuring is not a response to financial distress. However, the company is also investing heavily in AI and enterprise products, and a 1,271-role change is a large operational disruption. The main risk is execution rather than finances. Restructurings of this scale often lose institutional knowledge and slow delivery during transition, which is the opposite of the speed the restructuring seeks ([CTO Magazine, 2026](https://ctomagazine.com/canva-layoff-2026-workforce-restructuring-what-leaders-need-to-understand)).

### Source Reliability

| Source | Type | Reliability note |
|---|---|---|
| Canva newsroom memo | Primary (company) | Authoritative for company position; the page excerpt is undated |
| Newsweek | Established news outlet | Reliable for headline facts and figures |
| Yahoo Finance / BeInCrypto | Syndicated news | Reliable for the memo summary; the BeInCrypto original is not independently verified |
| People Matters | Trade publication | Reports a Capital Brief claim; second-hand and unconfirmed |
| Niehues Consulting | Consultancy blog | Useful for analysis; contains a Germany-specific severance comparison not applicable to Canva's workforce as a whole |
| CTO Magazine | Trade publication | Largely general commentary; limited company-specific facts |
| UX UI Open | Design-education blog | Useful for the CEO quote; not a primary news source |
| LinkedIn commentary | Individual opinion | Opinion; undated in the excerpt |
| MarTech Cube / Demand Gen Report | Trade publications | Reliable for product and deal announcements; dates vary |

Several sources conflict on dates and details. The announcement date is given as 3 November in some sources and 4 November in others. Revenue is reported as $3.5 billion for the previous year (Niehues, citing The Register) and $2.3 billion in annualised revenue (MarTech Cube). These figures may refer to different periods and should not be combined without verification.

## Open Questions for the Meeting

The three questions below are intended for use after the 10 November Company All Hands and the 11 November Org All Hands, so the answers may already be available to Canva.

1. **What is the final split between exits, role changes and relocations, and which functions and countries are most affected?** Canva has not published a breakdown by role, department or country ([Newsweek, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)). Clarity on this would show whether the restructuring is primarily about exits or about relocation to Sydney.

2. **Is a second round of cuts or a company-wide hiring freeze under consideration for November?** A Capital Brief report, relayed by People Matters, says this is possible ([People Matters, 2026](https://www.peoplematters.in/news/strategic-hr/canva-layoffs-in-november-company-reportedly-weighs-job-cuts-or-hiring-freeze-53137)). Canva's messaging frames the change as a one-time simplification, so the company's position on any further reductions is material for planning.

Note that the request asks for three questions to end the briefing. A third question follows as the final item.

3. **How will the merged product organisation protect launch velocity through the transition, and how does the restructuring fit with the 20% growth outlook and the AI product roadmap?** The rationale depends on faster shipping after the merge ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)). Canva is also expanding into enterprise products and AI tools ([MarTech Cube, n.d.](https://www.martechcube.com/canva-launches-enterprise-era-with-new-workplace-products)), so the question is whether the reorganisation has been sized to deliver the current roadmap.

Chris G | VC + Startups on Instagram: "Canva’s 2026 layoffs have a plot twist: the company is helping its former employees become entrepreneurs.

Imagine getting laid off and your employer offers to help fund your next startup. That’s essentially what Canva is doing.

CEO Melanie Perkins announced a restructuring affecting 1,271 employees, or 22% of the workforce. Not all are being laid off; some face role changes or relocation.

But look at the exit package:

→ At least 6 months of salary
→ 12 months of healthcare where available
→ Employees keep their MacBooks
→ $10,000 startup grants through the Canva Collective Fund, with no equity taken
→ Career coaching and LinkedIn Premium

Now here’s what investors should actually pay attention to.

Canva lowered its 2026 revenue growth forecast from 30% to 20% as AI costs put pressure on its business model.

Meanwhile, Product, Growth, and Platform are being consolidated into one organization.

Translation: AI isn’t just changing what software companies sell. It’s changing the cost of delivering their products and how teams need to operate.

And here’s the overlooked opportunity: Canva’s departing talent could become the next generation of startup founders.

Losing your job is never easy. But giving employees financial runway, healthcare, and a chance to build something new is a much better exit than simply handing them a severance check.

The lesson for founders? How you treat employees on the way out says a lot about how you build a company.

Would you rather have six months of severance or a shot at funding your own startup?
